name: Hong Kong
summary: Use the harbour as your anchor: Central, the Peak and a Star Ferry crossing make a strong first day. Give Lantau a separate outing rather than squeezing the Big Buddha between city stops.
seasonNote: Autumn often offers comfortable temperatures; summer heat, downpours and tropical cyclones can interrupt plans.
arrival: Airport Express serves major rail hubs; airport buses may be cheaper and closer to your hotel.
gettingAround: An Octopus card simplifies MTR, buses and ferries; walk short neighbourhood clusters.
cashTip: Carry small HKD notes for markets and older eateries; cards work well in larger venues.
foodTip: Try dim sum, wonton noodles, egg tarts and milk tea; many traditional dishes contain pork or shrimp.
buyTip: Buy tea, locally designed gifts or inexpensive market souvenirs; inspect quality before bargaining.
baseArea: Tsim Sha Tsui for harbour walks or Central/Sheung Wan for island access.

items.name: T'ang Court
items.summary: The Langham’s three-star Cantonese dining room: classic dim sum at lunch and refined banquet dishes at dinner.
items.expect: A long tasting-menu meal. Deposits, cancellation fees and smart-casual dress codes are common at this level.
items.tip: Book through the restaurant’s own site or official booking partner as soon as your dates are set.
items.priceNote: Per-person planning estimate from the MICHELIN price band ($$$), not a menu quote; drinks, service and tax may add to the total.
items.bestTime: Lunch or dinner by reservation; check the current service days

review.note: No verified review-count snapshot yet. The MICHELIN Guide entry is the source for this listing; open current reviews before booking.

whyVisit: The Langham’s three-star Cantonese dining room: classic dim sum at lunch and refined banquet dishes at dinner.
The MICHELIN Guide awards it Three MICHELIN Stars (exceptional cuisine), the guide’s highest award.
visitFlow: Book through the restaurant’s own site or official booking partner as soon as your dates are set.
Share allergies and dietary needs when booking; tasting menus are hard to change on the night.
Allow about three hours and plan a taxi or short walk back.
items.tradeoffs: Among the most expensive meals of a trip, and tables can sell out weeks or months ahead. Menus are set by the kitchen.

dietary.note: No dietary evidence collected yet. Ask the restaurant directly about halal, vegetarian and allergy needs; tasting menus need notice.
